payload.reason: One proposal (practice), selected as the core and checked against the survey, the investigation and five spikes. Three seams were changed: case-exact tag matching is now a precondition with its own rule and case, the live tag check is a one-reading P-004 instead of a C-052 extension, and the reading rule no longer narrows Q-178. Restart-only work is filed for a person.
payload.selection_rationale:
Only one design was proposed, from practice. Its designer raised over_engineering_flag against its own interest. I selected it as the core and checked each piece against what was measured. Nothing in it has yet survived a disagreement.

KEPT AS PROPOSED, AND WHY REALITY SUPPORTS IT
(1) The SC-130 reorder in Get-Missing. Spike sc130-guard-stop-survives-interrupt-fix went go:
- the bug test exits 0 in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7;
- control X2's line is byte-identical;
- eight fixture cases are byte-identical.

(2) The outcome-C redesign is a written record, not a judge. The investigation and three spikes characterise arm L's growth as first-touch NTFS/FltMgr metadata cache:
- a warm re-list keeps NtfF/NtxI/Ntfo at 0-2 on the host and exactly 0 in the Sandbox;
- deep memory pressure gave back 95-112% in two Sandbox runs;
- the app's open pattern costs the same per folder as a plain open.
The WC* leak is real and repeats on each walk (lesson #349). fitness.yaml:1097 already forbids verdicts in PoolWatch.

(3) No ScanArm, no absolute tolerance T, no standby purge:
- The VHD purge spike freed 0 of 261 NtfF. That contradicts the investigation's -2,460, so nothing may rest on a purge.
- Elevation is outside the PoolWatch stack.
- The tree's 6 GiB per-arm guard already is the 'safety cap well above the cache' that fix direction (c) asks for.
- The 2 GiB abort counted from R_start, and the judge that failed V3 on an empty L, lived only in scratch code that was never in the tree.

(4) Fourteen more watched tags. The extended-tags spike was no-go at 15 named tags (85.4% / 77.1% of paged growth). It named NtFs, FSim, MmSm and Ntf0 as the tags that lift coverage to 97.8%. The purge spike adds MmRe and Ntce. These tags must be in the harness before the person's one-shot Restart session, so they belong to this code slice and not to the measurement (lesson #344).

CHANGED FROM THE PROPOSAL, AGAINST REALITY
- Case-exact tag matching is made a precondition, with an architecture rule and a behavioural case (P-004). The host spike measured a case-insensitive hashtable merging NtfF with Ntff-like tags in exactly this kind of code. The two tags move in opposite directions: in the Sandbox, NtfF +6,981 while Ntff -7,226.
- The live Read-Mark check is a single reading in a new P-004 case instead of an extension of C-052. C-052 runs about 5 minutes, adds about +0.11 GB to a whole-machine pool counter that the engine guards at 0.5 GB (lesson #351), and builds a 30,150-folder tree in TEMP. Under the engine's TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP that tree leaves folders only an administrator can delete (lesson #391).
- The reading rule no longer drops File/MmSt/FMsl from Q-178's answered 'later scans add nothing'. It names NtfF and the WC columns as deciding, because their repeat noise was measured at about 0. Every other column is read against the same session's I0/I1 idle envelope. A design does not narrow an answered question.

WHAT REALITY STILL HAS TO SETTLE
Whether a warm full exe scan's SizeProbe pass nets about 0 NtfF (SC-230). It is recorded as the one decidable disagreement.

THE BUILD CHECK'S RESCOPE REQUEST
The build check asked for a person to rescope before design. Nobody can answer here. I took the rescope that lessons #344 and #357 and Q-184/Q-185 already imply:
- the code fix and the record are in this slice;
- both Restart sessions and the measurement-preparation code are filed for later;
- DONE (c) is checked_by person.

components.name: Get-Missing guard-stop branch
components.responsibility:
Judge an arm with guardStop set (and guardAtStart not set) BEFORE the interrupted branch at :460-465.
- It needs only <arm>/before and <arm>/exit.
- Each mark gets the same four field checks as :466-472: pagedBytes, nonpagedBytes, tags, system120089. A missing mark or field is named on its own line, and the guard line then ends 'its net at the stop is unread'. No net is ever made up.
- It prints the existing :473-478 wording: the guard reason, then the Get-Net net from /before to /exit.
- When interrupted is true, it appends '; then interrupted before its /settled mark', plus ' and killed' when killed is true.
- When interrupted is false and /settled is missing, it also prints 'mark <arm>/settled is missing'. This departs from the spike's version on purpose, so that a missing exit+10-minute reading stays visible.
- Then continue. The old guardStop branch at :473-478 becomes dead code and is deleted.
components.key_interactions:
- Get-Net (:512-520) and Write-RunReport (:558-559) are unchanged. An interrupted guard row still reads '(no net: a mark is missing)', because that table runs from /before to /settled.
- The guardAtStart cascade branch (:459) stays first.
- New strings are ASCII only, because Windows PowerShell 5.1 breaks double-quoted strings on non-ASCII dashes (lesson SL-059).
- New strings never match \b(PASS|FAIL|VOID|OUTCOME)\b (fitness.yaml:1097, PoolWatchCases.ps1:24).
- No new function, so no SL-098 return-value census row is needed.

components.name: Case-exact pool tag matching, then 14 more watched tags
components.responsibility:
STEP 1: make every pool-tag comparison in PoolWatch.ps1 case-exact.
- Use -ceq, -cne, -ccontains, -cin, -clike and -cmatch.
- Wherever tags key a lookup that is now an @{} hashtable, use a Dictionary built with [StringComparer]::Ordinal.
- The WC family becomes -clike 'WC*'.

STEP 2: add 14 names to $WatchedTags (:66), so Read-Mark records them in every mark: MmSt, MmCa, FMsl, FIcs, NtxI, Ntfo, Ntff, NtxF, NtFs, FSim, MmSm, Ntf0, MmRe, Ntce.

$NetTags and the -Report table columns stay as they are.
components.key_interactions:
- Read-Mark writes the tags array into marks.jsonl. Get-Net looks up $NetTags in that array, so it must match case-exactly too, or the NtfF column picks up Ntff.
- The 14 names come from two spikes. The extended-tags spike's run 3 reached 97.8% of paged growth with NtFs, FSim, MmSm and Ntf0 added. MmRe and Ntce were the purge spike's largest unnamed paged tags.
- Guarded by the architecture rule and by case P-004.
- Older logs and fixtures that lack the new names still read the same, because -Report never asks for them.

components.name: P-003 guard-stop arms
components.responsibility:
Add arms to P-003's fixture on plan arms that X3, F2 and F4 do not use.
- (a) guardStop 'available 2900 MB, pool +310 MiB over <arm>/before', exitCode -1, interrupted true, killed false; /before and /exit present, no /settled. Expect the reason, 'paged +310 MiB ... from /before to /exit', and '; then interrupted before its /settled mark'.
- (b) Same as (a) with killed true. Expect ' and killed'.
- (c) guardStop, interrupted true, exitCode null, no /exit. Expect the missing /exit named, 'its net at the stop is unread', and no MiB figure for that arm.
- (d) guardStop, not interrupted; /before and /exit present, no /settled. Expect the guard line and 'mark <arm>/settled is missing'.
The X3, F2 and F4 expectations do not change. The 5-full / 5-cancel plan stays valid.
components.key_interactions:

- This is SC-130's standing regression. It meets the build-check criterion 'P-003 carries an arm with guardStop, interrupted true, killed false and exitCode -1'.

key_decisions.decision: In Get-Missing, judge guardStop before interrupted. The guard branch needs only /before and /exit, prints the reason and the /before-to-/exit net, and adds 'then interrupted' (and ' and killed') as a suffix. It never replaces the guard line. The dead :473-478 branch is deleted.
key_decisions.rationale: Proven by spike sc130: the bug test exits 0 in 5.1 and 7, X2 is byte-identical and 8 fixture cases are byte-identical. The net at the stop is the only figure a guard-stopped arm is sure to have.

key_decisions.decision: A guard-stopped arm that was NOT interrupted and has no /settled mark still prints 'mark <arm>/settled is missing'. The spike's variant V4 dropped this line.
key_decisions.rationale: Backlog item 4 asks for the exit+10-minute reading of a guard-stopped arm, so its absence must stay visible. Neither X2 nor C-056's guard arm lacks /settled: X2's raw-net row reads /before to /settled, and C-056 was byte-identical under the spike's version. So the acceptance test and every existing fixture are unaffected.

key_decisions.decision: Make every pool-tag comparison in PoolWatch.ps1 case-exact before adding the 14 tags. Then record MmSt, MmCa, FMsl, FIcs, NtxI, Ntfo, Ntff, NtxF, NtFs, FSim, MmSm, Ntf0, MmRe and Ntce by name in every mark. Do not record the whole tag table, and leave $NetTags and the -Report columns unchanged.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike 87 left about 172 MiB unattributed, and the named set reaches 97.8% of paged growth in the Sandbox. The whole table (about 3,600 tags) would be about 300 KB per mark, committed under docs/design/<slice>-runs/. Case-exactness comes first because NtfF and Ntff are distinct tags that move in opposite directions, PowerShell folds case by default, and the host spike already hit this merge.

key_decisions.decision: Treat arm L's growth as Windows' first-touch file-system metadata cache. Do not change Scanner.cs or DirectoryReader.cs for it, and add no KnownWorkarounds entry. Keep the Layers exclusion (Scanner.cs:66, DirectoryReader.cs:84-96) and the wcifs-layer-store precaution unchanged.
key_decisions.rationale: No outside defect is being stepped around here. The investigation found the cost is designed caching that is given back under deep pressure, and that the app's open costs the same as a plain open (Sandbox: NtfF +6,981 against +6,533 allocations). The wcifs leak is the one real outside defect, and it already has its own checkbox. Reversing this decision means a scanner-tier slice with counting-rule tests. It rests on Sandbox-scale evidence and 3,000 host folders; host-scale release is SC-231.

key_decisions.decision:
Read session 1 by Q-178's own conditions, using the five identical full scans the protocol already runs:
- F1 is the cold scan; F2-F5 are warm repeats.
- NtfF and the WC columns decide, because their repeat noise was measured at about 0.
- Every other column is reported and read against the same session's idle envelope.
No tolerance T, no standby purge, no deep-pressure step, and no judge in PoolWatch.
key_decisions.rationale: A single cold pass against an absolute T is what counted reclaimable cache as damage in spike 87. A cache is paid once and a leak is paid on every pass; the project's own WC evidence has that shape (+5 per repeat walk). The purge is contested by two measurements and needs elevation. Deep pressure cannot be produced on a 32 GB host. This rule operationalises Q-178 (3) and leaves Q-178 (1) and (2) intact. Changing it after the session costs another true Restart.

key_decisions.decision: ScanArm and the L/S/P arms do not come back. PoolWatch drives the published exe only, and the 6 GiB per-arm guard with the 3072 MB Available floor is the safety cap.
key_decisions.rationale: The listing cost that L was built to isolate is now characterised directly. The F arms include the SizeProbe half, so a separate S arm is not needed. Rebuilding the rig would repeat SL-095's ten design rounds, and the stack line already deletes ScanArm once O-003 is decided.

key_decisions.decision: Split the work. This slice builds the harness fix, the tags and the record. Filed for later: session 1 and session 2 (Q-185's dir /a /s) for a person, and a measurement-preparation slice (Y3 without verdict words, readings around the dir commands, a guard-trip rehearsal, a reader for the new tags). DONE (c) is checked_by person.
key_decisions.rationale: Lessons #344 and #357: a whole-C: run after a Restart cannot close on loop evidence, and the engine's 0.5 GB whole-machine guard forbids it unattended. The build check asked a person to rescope; with nobody to answer, this is the rescope those lessons and Q-184/Q-185 already imply.

key_decisions.decision: Prove the live Read-Mark path with one reading in the new case P-004, loaded from PoolWatch.ps1 by the parser. Do not extend C-052.
key_decisions.rationale: One reading takes about 0.4 s with negligible pool. C-052 takes about 5 minutes and +0.11 GB (lesson #351), and its 30,150-folder tree leaves admin-only folders under the engine's TEMP (lesson #391). The fallback, if the parser load is impractical, is C-052 run alone under a committed TEMP wrapper.

key_decisions.decision:
Close backlog items 3 and 4 on the record, not on new code.
- Item 3: the R_start abort and the empty-L judge were scratch-only. The tree's live harness fault was SC-130, which this slice fixes.
- Item 4, first half: the harness already writes /exit and /settled after a guard stop; taking the reading is the person's session.
- Item 4, second half: closed on what bab35f3 committed. The rest is recorded as unrecoverable.
key_decisions.rationale: The build check found the faulty rig was never tracked, and the run folder holds only L\. The record says what cannot be checked again, rather than restating those figures as measured.

key_decisions.decision: Leave PoolWatchCases.ps1's scratch roots as they are. Run fixture cases directly, as the build check did, and never run C-052 under the engine's TEMP.
key_decisions.rationale: Lesson #391 lists PoolWatchCases among the scripts that are red under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. Yet the build check measured all 9 fixture cases at exit 0, and a measurement outranks the lesson for those cases. Fixing every scratch root is SL-098's class of work and is filed for later.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal (practice), so there is no composition across proposals to check. Nothing here has survived a disagreement; the reviewer downstream is the first to argue with it. These are the internal seams that were checked, and what was changed.

1. THE PROPOSAL'S DEPARTURE FROM THE SPIKE'S PROVEN FIX
The proposal keeps 'mark X/settled is missing' for a guard-stopped arm that was not interrupted. Checked against the acceptance test and the fixtures:
- X2 carries /settled (its raw-net row reads 2.0 MiB from /before to /settled).
- C-056 was byte-identical under the spike's version, so its guard arm has /settled too.
So restoring the pre-fix line for that one shape changes no existing output. Kept, and pinned as a P-003 arm.

2. CASE-EXACT MATCHING AGAINST OLDER LOGS AND FIXTURES
Fixtures spell tags exactly, so their output should not move; case 8 checks that by running every fixture case. Committed SL-095-runs logs lack the 14 new names, but -Report never asks for them. If 0feac0e folded case, earlier NtfF and WC figures may include case variants; the record must say so (record item i).

3. READING RULE AGAINST fitness.yaml:1097 (NO VERDICT IN POOLWATCH)
The rule lives in the doc and is read by a person, so there is no conflict.

4. READING RULE AGAINST ANSWERED QUESTIONS Q-178, Q-184 AND Q-185 — CHANGED
The proposal said File, MmSt and FMsl 'are not read'. That narrows Q-178's 'later scans add nothing', which is an answered decision. Redesigned: NtfF and the WC columns decide, and every other column is still read against the session's own idle envelope. Q-178 (1) and (2) are left untouched.

5. READING RULE AGAINST THE 6 GiB PER-ARM GUARD
A guard-stopped F1 leaves no cold baseline. The record says that F2-F5 are then read only among themselves.

6. LIVE TAG CHECK — CHANGED
The proposal's C-052 extension would build a 30,150-folder tree in TEMP. Under the engine's C:\WINDOWS\TEMP that tree is undeletable (lesson #391), and the run adds +0.11 GB to a 0.5 GB whole-machine guard (lesson #351). Replaced by a one-reading P-004.

7. MEASUREMENT AGAINST LESSON
Lesson #391 says PoolWatchCases is red under the engine's TEMP. The build check measured 9 fixture cases at exit 0. The measurement stands for fixture cases; only C-052, which builds a tree in TEMP, is kept off the engine's TEMP.

8. ARCHITECTURE RULE AGAINST HEAD
If HEAD's PoolWatch.ps1 compares tags with case-folding operators, the rule goes red on appending. That is intended: the build converts those lines before adding Ntff and NtxF. The c-prefixed correct forms cannot match the patterns, because each pattern needs the operator letters to follow the '-' directly.

9. NO NEW OUTSIDE-DEFECT WORKAROUND
The listing cost is designed caching, so no KnownWorkarounds entry is added. The existing wcifs-layer-store entry and its checkbox are untouched. The one-checkbox-per-defect list is therefore unchanged.

architecture_rules.name: PoolWatch never compares pool tag names without regard to case
architecture_rules.because: Pool tags are case-sensitive 4-byte values, and NtfF/Ntff and NtxI/NtxF are distinct live tags that move in opposite directions (Sandbox small folders: NtfF +6,981 allocations while Ntff -7,226). PowerShell's default operators fold case. Once this slice watches Ntff and NtxF, a case-folding comparison silently merges them into NtfF, the column the outcome-C reading decides on. The host-repeat spike already hit this merge. The c-prefixed forms (-ccontains, -cin, -clike, -ceq) are the correct ones and cannot match these patterns.

contracts.name: PoolWatch.ps1 -Report: MISSING line for a guard-stopped arm
contracts.notes:
Line format:
'  MISSING arm <X>: stopped by the machine guard (<reason>): paged ±N MiB, nonpaged ±N MiB from /before to /exit[; then interrupted before its /settled mark[ and killed]]'
- Exit code 2 for an incomplete run is unchanged.
- The guardAtStart cascade line keeps its own earlier branch.
- Strings are ASCII and contain no PASS/FAIL/VOID/OUTCOME.
contracts.error_cases:
- /before or /exit is missing, or one of its four fields is null: one line names it, and the guard line ends 'its net at the stop is unread'. No figure is printed.
- Not interrupted and /settled missing: an extra line, 'mark <X>/settled is missing'.
- Interrupted with no guardStop: the :460-465 wording is unchanged.
contracts.auth_model: Unelevated. Reads the run's JSONL files only.

contracts.name: marks.jsonl tags array written by Read-Mark
contracts.notes: Additive: 14 more named tags per mark, alongside WC*, FMwi, FMfc, FMfn, File, NtfF and Toke. Tag names are compared case-exactly everywhere. Older logs without the new tags read the same, because $NetTags and the -Report columns are unchanged.
contracts.error_cases:
- An absent tag is treated exactly as the existing watched tags are today.
- Tags that differ only in case are never merged.
- A WC entry is any tag beginning case-exactly with 'WC'.

contracts.name: PoolWatchCases.ps1 -Case P-003 and -Case P-004

- P-003: fixture only, under 1 s, with four new guard-stop arms beside X3, F2 and F4.
- P-004: a fixture half, plus one live reading through PoolWatch.ps1's own Read-Mark, loaded by the parser.
- P-004 is added to the ValidateSet (:17) and to the All list (:375).

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Leak testing in managed runtimes: iterate an identical workload after a warm-up pass and check retained growth (LeakCanary / dotMemory Unit / Valgrind practice)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Tell a leak from a cache by the slope across identical repetitions after the first pass, not by one pass against an absolute tolerance. Use a forced-reclaim step only where it is known to reclaim.

invariants.precondition: The repetitions are the same workload: F1-F5 run the same published exe on the same root with the same options.
invariants.evidence: Invoke-Protocol :603-615 runs plan, R0, I0, F1-F5, X1-X5 and I1. exe-full requires notScanned ≥ 1 and opensUnderExcludedStore 0. Nobody has read whether the arguments are identical across the F arms; the build reads it.
-Protocol refuses unless it starts within 30 minutes of boot (:690-691). Only a person can give a true Start > Restart.

invariants.precondition: The cache F1 builds survives to F2-F5, so no eviction re-grows it and looks like a leak.
invariants.evidence: The host has about 17 GB standby and 16.7 GB available. In the Sandbox, moderate pressure released nothing (NtfF 0); only deep pressure did. The 6 GiB per-arm guard and the 3072 MB Available floor keep the session far from deep pressure.

invariants.precondition: On the deciding tags, a listing-only warm repeat stays within noise.
invariants.evidence: Host-repeat spike, gate-passed runs 4-6: NtfF, NtxI and Ntfo were 0-2 on every warm repeat, against +57 to +136 on the first pass. File, MmSt and FMsl breached the 10% bound by 9-47 counts, so they do not decide.

invariants.precondition: A warm repeat of the SizeProbe pass also nets about 0 on NtfF.
invariants.evidence: The spike's probe half (C2 against C1) was void, and FileRepository's cold sets are used up on this boot (SC-230). This is recorded as the decidable disagreement.

invariants.precondition: A real per-pass leak shows up as growth on each repetition.
invariants.evidence: Lesson #349: +5 WCsc/WCfc/WCri/FMwi and +5 System 0x120089 handles on each of 4 repeat walks of Files\Windows\Globalization.

invariants.precondition: A forced-reclaim step reliably frees the cache, so it can serve as a second discriminator.
invariants.evidence: Sandbox purge spike, 400x40 on VHD: the purge freed 0 of 261 NtfF, and the third listing found the set warm. The deep-pressure release holds only at 4 GB Sandbox scale (SC-231). Not used.

prior_art.pattern: Find a kernel pool leak by watching per-tag pool bytes and allocations over time and attributing growth to tags (PoolMon). This is the same unit as PoolWatch's marks.

On Windows 11 25H2, first-time (cold) file-name operations each keep about 1 KB of pool (FMfn, File, NtfF, FMsl, MmSt), warm paths add nothing, and nothing is released while memory is plentiful. This is the same signature as arm L.

Killing the triggering process tree frees its committed memory but not the FltMgr/File/IoFE pool it caused. A reading taken after the process exits measures Windows' retained state, not the app's own memory.
Take a baseline of normal pool usage before treating growth as a leak, then attribute it per tag with poolmon.
Leak tests iterate an identical workload after a warm-up and flag retained growth that scales with the number of iterations. A one-time cost after the first pass is not a leak.
prior_art.where: LeakCanary / JetBrains dotMemory Unit / Valgrind memcheck practice

prior_art.pattern: RAMMap 'Empty Standby List' (NtSetSystemInformation SystemMemoryListInformation, MemoryPurgeStandbyList) used as a cache flush before re-measuring pool. In this project it did not release NtfF on VHD.
PowerShell's -eq, -contains, -in, Group-Object and @{} keys ignore case by default. Case-sensitive work needs -ceq/-ccontains/-cmatch or a dictionary built with [StringComparer]::Ordinal.

outside_claims.claim: PowerShell's -eq, -ne, -contains, -in, -like and -match compare strings without regard to case by default. The c-prefixed forms (-ceq, -ccontains, -cin, -clike, -cmatch) are case-sensitive.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The architecture rule's patterns would target the wrong operators. The P-004 fixture half still catches a merged NtfF/Ntff behaviourally.

outside_claims.source: spike host-repeat-listing-keeps-no-pool: 'a case-insensitive hashtable merged NtfF with Ntff-like tags' (an analysis bug found and fixed there)
outside_claims.if_wrong: Case-exactness would be less urgent. The rule and P-004 would still be harmless.

decidable_disagreements.question: Does a warm repeat of a full exe scan (SizeProbe on every file the default ProbeRule selects) net about 0 on NtfF and the WC columns from /before to /settled, as a listing-only repeat does?
decidable_disagreements.positions:
The design assumes yes, extrapolating the host-repeat spike's listing half (NtfF, NtxI and Ntfo 0-2 on every warm repeat).

Reality has no valid answer yet:
- the spike's probe half (C2 against C1) was void, and FileRepository's cold sets are used up on this boot (SC-230);
- lesson #349 attributes a repeating +5 WC per walk to SizeProbe opens of reparse+sparse ICU files (unconfirmed). That would be the rule working, not failing.

The losing case: per-file FCBs are torn down and re-made on each pass without a cap, so NtfF nets non-zero from churn. The F1-against-F2..F5 rule then cannot tell cache from leak on NtfF. The record's discriminator would have to change, for example by bringing back a listing-only repeat arm, which is a new arm type in Invoke-Protocol.

The question can be settled in the Sandbox on created files, or by the person's session 1.

taste_disagreements: Spike sc130's fix stopped printing 'mark X/settled is missing' for a guard-stopped arm that was not interrupted (variant V4). This design keeps that line. Neither choice changes the acceptance test or any existing fixture.
The 'then interrupted' note is a suffix on the guard line. A separate line would satisfy the acceptance test equally ('may be added but must not replace them').
The tag-case check is a new case, P-004, which costs two list edits at :17 and :375. The alternative was folding it into P-003, a case about interrupted arms.
A new record, docs/design/SL-099-outcome-c-redesign.md, plus a one-line pointer, against rewriting SL-095's hand-off section in place.
A named 21-tag set in each mark, against the whole ~3,600-tag table at about 300 KB per mark.
NtfF and the WC columns as the deciding columns, because their repeat noise was measured at about 0, against reading Q-178's FMfn/File/NtfF trio as decisive.
